title: Pan Am 103
summary: Pan Am Flight 103, a Boeing 747 flying from Frankfurt to Detroit via London and New York, was destroyed by a bomb while cruising over Lockerbie, Scotland, on 21 December 1988, killing all 259 aboard and 11 people on the ground. Investigators found the explosion tore a hole in the fuselage, the nose was blown off within seconds, and disrupted elevator and rudder cables caused the aircraft to break apart; Abdelbaset al-Megrahi was convicted of the bombing in 2001.
probable_cause: Investigators concluded a bomb concealed in the cargo hold exploded in flight, tearing open the fuselage and severing flight control cables, causing the aircraft to break up over Lockerbie; Libyan intelligence officer Abdelbaset al-Megrahi was convicted of 270 counts of murder for the bombing in 2001.

events.text: Shortly after 19:00 GMT on 21 December 1988 the Boeing 747 Clipper Maid of the Seas was destroyed by a bomb while flying over the Scottish town of Lockerbie.
The explosion tore a 50 cm hole in the left side of the fuselage, ripping the upper deck walls and roof away within the first few seconds.
No distress call was recorded; a 180-millisecond hissing noise was captured on the cockpit voice recorder as the explosion destroyed the aircraft's communications center.
Within three seconds the nose of the aircraft was blown off and separated from the fuselage, briefly held on by a band of metal before shearing off and striking the number-three engine.

The elevator- and rudder-control cables were disrupted and the fuselage pitched downwards and to the left as the aircraft broke apart and fell near Lockerbie, killing all 259 aboard and 11 on the ground.
